sources.title: NGSS 5-ESS2-2: Describe and graph the amounts of salt water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth
OpenStax Biology 2e, 46.3 Biogeochemical Cycles (where Earth's water is stored)

legend.name: Ice and underground
legend.meaning: Fresh water frozen or deep in the ground

steps.title: First graph
steps.instruction: Trace the axes of the first graph.

note.text: This bar graph splits all of Earth's water into salt water and fresh water.

steps.title: Salt water
steps.instruction: Trace the tall salt water bar.

note.text: 97.5% of Earth's water is salt water, mostly in the ocean. We can't drink it.

steps.title: Fresh water
steps.instruction: Trace the tiny fresh water bar.

note.text: Only 2.5% is fresh water. That's about 1 cup out of every 40.

steps.title: Second graph
steps.instruction: Trace the axes of the second graph.

note.text: This graph zooms in on just the fresh water. Where is it?
About 99% of fresh water is frozen in ice or stored underground, where it's hard to reach.

steps.title: Lakes and rivers
steps.instruction: Trace the thin bar for lakes and rivers.

note.text: Less than 1% of fresh water is easy to reach in lakes and rivers. Many living things depend on it.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: Color the bars. The lakes and rivers bar is too thin to fill.

steps.title: Read the graph
steps.question: Where is most of Earth's water?

options.text: In the ocean, as salt water
options.feedback: Yes. 97.5% of all Earth's water is salt water.
Lakes and rivers hold less than 1% of the fresh water, a tiny part of the total.
Clouds hold very little. Almost all water, 97.5%, is salt water in the ocean.
Ice holds most fresh water, but fresh water is only 2.5% of all water.

steps.title: Use the evidence
steps.question: Why is it important not to waste fresh water?

options.text: Only a tiny part of Earth's water is fresh and easy to reach
options.feedback: Right. Fresh water is 2.5% of the total, and less than 1% of that is in lakes and rivers.

options.text: Fresh water is most of Earth's water
options.feedback: Look at the first graph: fresh water is only 2.5%.

options.text: Salt water is easy to drink
options.feedback: We can't drink salt water, which is why fresh water is so precious.

options.text: All fresh water is in rivers
options.feedback: Most fresh water is locked in ice or underground. Less than 1% is in lakes and rivers.
